ai_show_review.summary: Jam‑heavy early set with strong Morning Dew and Viola Lee Blues
ai_show_review.blurb: The three‑song set opens with a fiery rendition of Morning Dew, moves into an expansive Viola Lee Blues jam, and closes with a modest Good Morning Little Schoolgirl. The performance captures the raw, drum‑circle energy of early ’67, though the lo‑fi soundboard tape limits clarity.
ai_show_review.review: On January 14, 1967 at the Fillmore Auditorium the Dead delivered a brief but intense three‑song set that feels more like a communal jam session than a polished concert. Morning Dew erupts with gritty guitar and vocal urgency, segueing into a sprawling Viola Lee Blues where Bill Kreutzmann’s drumming drives a hypnotic rhythm while Pigpen’s organ adds a swampy texture. The set closes with Good Morning Little Schoolgirl, which, while less inspired, still showcases the band’s early‑stage chemistry. This is the only surviving soundboard capture of the night; despite its modest fidelity it remains the most complete document of this formative period.

best_recording.reason: Only existing soundboard capture; despite lo‑fi fidelity it provides the most complete and balanced representation of the three‑song set.

key_highlights: Solid, jam‑heavy performances of Morning Dew and Viola Lee Blues.
Early ’67 raw energy feels like a drum‑circle session.
Lo‑fi tape limits clarity but preserves the historic vibe.
